title: Stitch prefetch + kernel routing: reduce CPU-GPU pipeline tail and copy churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: cut host-side CPU overhead and memory-copy churn during prefill->decode pipelines by redesigning kernel selection and prefetch orchestration.

Scope: implement a lightweight "stitch" router that: 1) chooses the least-cost kernel variant per micro-batch (fused vs unfused attention, rotary/rope path, quantized kernels), 2) co-schedules prefill DMA/pinning and KV-cache warmup to avoid synchronous copies during decode, 3) assigns work to NUMA-aware thread pools with token-aware throttling to reduce contention.

Success metrics (target):
- 25% reduction in host CPU p95 during steady-state generation
- 15% reduction in p99 token latency on typical 8k-context workloads
- <=5% regression in token throughput for high-batch workloads (prefer no regression)

Non-goals: full rewrite of kernel runtime; no model layout changes. Focus is on router + scheduling changes that fit into existing runtime hooks.
comments: 2026-02-18 — Spike complete: microbench harness for kernel variants created (bench/kernels/variant_harness). Measured per-kernel init cost, fused-attention amortization point is ~16 tokens for our Llama-2-13B profile.

2026-02-24 — Prototype router implemented. It picks between fused attention, split attention, and int8-quantized kernels based on sequence length, batch size, and current GPU occupancy. Initial end-to-end runs show 18% host CPU reduction on p50 and 12% p95 improvement for 4k sequences on dev infra.

2026-03-02 — Memory copy experiment: introduced a pinned-buffer staging pool + async DMA submission during prefill. Observed cut in synchronous host->GPU memcpy peaks by 60% in internal lab traces. However, some workloads saw higher tail due to threadpool contention when many small requests arrive concurrently.

2026-03-04 — Threadpool mitigation: split the host scheduler into two pools: prefill-pool (affined to NUMA node 0) and decode-pool (affined to NUMA node 1). Added a token-aware queue that prioritizes warmup tasks for KV-heavy requests. Result: p99 host CPU dropped further; contention hotspots on mutexes decreased by ~40% in flamegraphs.

2026-03-06 — Canary run on staging (dedicated-2 region): Canary showed median latency improvements consistent with lab, p99 improved 11% on mixed workloads. One customer test (large prompt streaming) regressed throughput by 7% under synthetic load due to conservative kernel switch thresholds. Re-tuning required.

2026-03-09 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345 — includes router, pinned-pool, and threadpool partitioning. Needs review: fallback for kernels that fail to compile at runtime, and telemetry hooks for kernel-choice tracing.

Next steps — (1) Add per-model autotune pass that learns kernel-choice threshold for each workload profile, (2) Add safety-fallback that sends failing kernels to a low-priority compile queue, (3) Instrument per-request kernel trace in console for rollout visibility, (4) Run 48-hour soak on dedicated clusters before release-flagging.
